issue: Some navigation recovery rules were rendered as re-observation rather than a native Back action; a real manual overlay-button tap could also dispatch Back without returning to the preceding page.
changes: Map typed BACK recovery rules to the existing native Back recovery.
Keep a real observed native Back control usable when a Settings page title is unavailable.
Expose the recovery panel and button even if the input menu was open.
Use explicit button instructions in manual mode.
Hide the touched guidance window and wait 120ms before revalidating the same native Settings window and dispatching Back.
Restore the guidance window only for the same session, generation and presentation; reobserve the returned page without restarting the task.

validation.manual_test: Production recovery presenter rendered a visible Back button; a real injected screen touch executed native Back from Connections to the preceding Settings home.
validation.automatic_test: Production recovery presenter automatically executed native Back over the same controlled Settings detour.
validation.before_manual_fix: On the same physical device, manual Back was dispatched once but did not return; automatic Back passed.
limits: Detour setup used native Settings intents and a controlled in-memory task with no Backend gateway.
Tests establish native navigation and UI action behavior; they are not an end-to-end model accuracy measurement.
